batch: WP-15, first batch (the final audits' Stage 4, alongside track)
rules: A claim is written as narrative.js's STATEMENT_CLAIMS writes it ({h, cl, by, note}); h is tools/step4/statements.js hashOf of the statement's label and text. A correction's claim carries the hash of the corrected statement. appearanceSources: none (every work cited is in APPEARANCE_SOURCES).

proposals.text: Napoleon has deliberately given up the Pratzen plateau and left his right, along the lower Goldbach, looking thin enough to invite attack. Weyrother's Allied orders, read out at Krzenowitz after midnight to commanders who largely did not understand them, send four of five columns south-west across the French front. Fog fills the Goldbach valley. Soult's two assault divisions are standing in it, invisible from the heights.
proposals.why: Each part of the lede rests on a reading made on a page image, but for three of its words. 'Read out ... after midnight' is this map's precision for Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky's account (Weyrother explained the disposition on a plan of the ground toward the middle of the night), which the note gives; the place is Kutuzov's quarters, the headquarters at Krzenowitz in Stutterheim; 'south-west' is this map's bearing. Thiébault's p. 457, read again here for the fog, also has Napoleon say on 21 November that he would refuse his right by drawing it back toward Brünn (not part of the registered quotation).

claim.note: Marbot calls the thin right a trap; Stutterheim has the French draw their outposts back to the villages on the stream and the Allied headquarters at Krzenowitz; Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky has Weyrother explain the disposition to the column chiefs at Kutuzov's toward the middle of the night, before its Russian translation, and Sokolov has many commanders understand their routes poorly; the disposition sends four of its five columns against the French right by villages, not by a bearing, so south-west is this map's. Thiébault has the fog hide the French in the valleys.

proposals.text: Ten kilometres of open Moravian farmland. The French army, marked in blue, is to the west; to the east are the Russians and the Austrians, marked in amber. Between them runs the Goldbach, a small stream in its valley, and behind it stands the Pratzen plateau, the high ground in the centre of the field.
proposals.why: The geography is Stutterheim's (A). 'Ten kilometres' is the distance from the Santon to Telnitz in GEOREF's frame, 10.15 km (derived here with GEOREF.kmBetween); 'open Moravian farmland' is not in a passage read.

claim.note: Stutterheim has the Allies on the heights between Aujest, Pratzen and Holubitz and the defiles of Telnitz, Sokolnitz and Schlapanitz between the two armies; he names the stream's defiles, not the stream. The field's breadth is measured on this map, from the Santon to Telnitz, and the colours are its convention.

proposals.text: At about a quarter to nine Saint-Hilaire and Vandamme climb out of the fog onto a plateau the Allies are leaving. Two divisions, the Guard held back, against a column still filing off the heights.
proposals.why: The opening's second step. Its hour is the map's choice inside a disputed range (EVENTS[#soult].dispute, since the final audits' Stage 2, names Ségur's, Thiébault's, Stutterheim's and Schönhals's hours); the note says so without a clock time, as test.js requires.

claim.note: The 30th Bulletin sends Soult onto the heights of Pratzen with Vandamme's and Saint-Hilaire's divisions and says no man of the reserve, the Guard's battalions and the grenadiers, was engaged; Thiébault has the fog hide them in the valley; Stutterheim and Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky have the 4th Column still on the plateau. The hour is this map's, inside the range the sources read give (the climb's event names each side).

proposals.text: The French centre turns ninety degrees and comes down off the heights into the rear of the Allied left. A way out for them is the neck of dry ground at Augezd, under guns on ground the Allies held at dawn.
proposals.why: The opening's last step. Its first sentence is in the sources; its second is the reading PHASES[#8].lede already calls this map's ('This map reads it as a way left open'), so the claim is this map's reading, with the readings that bound it.

claim.note: Marbot has the Emperor come down from the Pratzen with Soult's corps and the Guard and take the Allied columns in the rear while Davout attacks them in front; Schönhals has the guns of IV Corps and of the Guard on the height above the retreat. That the neck of dry ground at Augezd was a way out is this map's reading: the disposition's retreat for the left ran through Kobelnitz and Puntowitz, and the army's, should the attack fail outright, on Niemtschan, Hodjegitz and Herspitz. The ninety degrees are this map's geometry.

proposals.text: Weyrother's orders send four of the five Allied columns south-west, off the plateau, to turn the French right and cut the road to Vienna. The heavy arrows are the intended lines of march. Note what they all have in common: they lead away from the centre.
proposals.why: The tour's second stop.

Cutting the road to Vienna is the aim Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky gives the Allied command's resolution after Wischau, not a phrase of the disposition.

proposals.text: Kienmayer's Austrian advance guard attacks Telnitz, the southernmost village on the Goldbach. Legrand's thin line holds the buildings and the vineyard bank above them, and the village changes hands repeatedly. Behind Kienmayer, Dokhturov's I Column is coming down off the southern end of the plateau.
proposals.why: Every part is in a reading made on a page image but the two words the note names.

claim.note: Stutterheim has the 3rd Line and two battalions of skirmishers in Telnitz and its vineyards, the height before the village taken, the village entered and lost again, and the I Column slow to come up; Sokolov puts the 3rd Line in Legrand's division; Davout reports the village taken and retaken. 'Thin' and 'the southernmost village on the Goldbach' are this map's words.

proposals.text: Langeron and Przybyszewski attack Sokolnitz village, its castle and the pheasantry beyond. On the plateau the 4th Column, which was meant to replace the troops leaving the heights, is still standing still: Liechtenstein's cavalry has cut across its line of march. A gap opens between it and the 3rd Column.
proposals.why: The phase title (by class) and nine other statements name the pheasantry (listed below); this correction drops it from the lede only. The data task may instead keep it as 'and, as this map draws it from the survey of 1825, the pheasantry beyond'.
proposals.unresolved: 'the 4th Column, which was meant to replace the troops leaving the heights' is contradicted by the disposition read: the 4th Column too marches off by the left through the places named and aligns with the first three (S8.6), toward Kobelnitz (Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky, S8.9, C1.9); and 'the pheasantry' is in none of the accounts read (this batch searched the text layers of the sixteen works it downloaded for 'Fasan', 'faisan' and 'фазан' and found none; the audit after Stage 8 found it in none of the 1805-1806 texts, CL-GEO-02). This map draws the pheasantry from the cadastral sketch of 1825 (decision 259 (a)); whether it stood, and was enclosed, in 1805 is among SOURCE_NOTE's open questions.

bearsOnWP03.readings: S8.12 (Stutterheim p. 39: on the evening of 1 December the Guard's reserve corps took post forward of Austerlitz, its left toward Krzenowitz and its right toward the Austerlitz-Brünn high road); S8.7 (the disposition, p. 106: behind Blasowitz and Kruh at daybreak, also C1.1); S8.9 (Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky p. 233: the Guard ready to reinforce Bagration); S8.2 (Sokolov p. 36: the Russian Guard formed a little west of Austerlitz).

bearsOnWP03.item: Legrand's route after 08:00 (Levasseur's brigade only?) and who held Sokolnitz village
bearsOnWP03.readings: S8.1 (Sokolov p. 35: at dawn Levasseur's brigade at Kobelnitz, Merle's at Sokolnitz and Telnitz); S8.10 (Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky p. 243: the French driven from the castle; Wimpfen's Podolia, Azov and Narva regiments the reserve on the Allied side of the stream).

S8.11 (Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky, French translation, p. 253: Kamensky reports to Langeron, as he nears the Goldbach, that the French are climbing the Pratzen heights and that the Phanagoria and Ryazhsk regiments cannot follow toward Sokolnitz; Kutuzov withdraws with Kamensky's brigade toward Hostieradek after ordering Buxhowden to retire).

S8.7 (the disposition, p. 106: in the worst case the army retires on Niemtschan, Hodjegitz and Herspitz) and S8.9 (Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky p. 233: on Kodiegitz, on the road to Hungary); C6.11 (Stutterheim p. 71, read again here: Bagration to the Rausnitz heights as the Guard left the heights behind Blasowitz, behind Austerlitz in the evening).
